newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRA reported to rule out pre-poll truce.
newsitem.headline: IRA reported to rule out pre-poll truce.

text.p: The Irish Republican Army (IRA) was reported on Friday to have ruled out a new ceasefire ahead of British and Irish elections which must be held within the next three months.
The Northern Ireland guerrilla organisation told correspondents from the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) and Ireland's RTE network that a new truce was "most unlikely."

The IRA, which seeks to end British rule of Northern Ireland to unite it with the Irish republic, said it was committed to a peace settlement which allowed its Sinn Fein political wing to take part in peace talks without preconditions.

The briefing was given to the two organisations on the eve of the anniversary of February 9, 1996, collapse of a 17-month IRA truce, when the guerrillas carried out a bombing in the Docklands business and residential development area in the east end of London, killing two people.
Sinn Fein is barred from Belfast peace talks because of the IRA's guerrilla war.
